 Milton, Pa. — DIG Furniture Bank’s annual Merry + Bright Market will double as a moving sale this year, as the nonprofit prepares to leave its longtime Milton home.
 The market runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, at DIG’s current location, 14 Elm St. in Milton. Admission is free and open to the public.
 Past DIG clients can shop free of charge, with an exclusive early window from 10 a.m. to noon and free shopping continuing until 4 p.m. All past clients are welcome regardless of when they received DIG’s services. Names will be verified at the door using DIG’s client database, and guests may be asked to show identification. Item limits may apply, and all merchandise is available while supplies last.
 The general public can shop at affordable prices from noon to 4 p.m. Proceeds from public purchases support DIG’s mission of providing furniture and household essentials to local families in need.
 Along with Christmas trees, ornaments, wreaths, lights and other seasonal decorations, shoppers will find furniture, household goods and other surplus items DIG will not be taking to its new location.
 The event will also feature snacks, entertainment, children’s activities and a client-only Santa’s Secret Workshop, where clients can select new toys and gifts for loved ones, with gift-wrapping available. The market is sponsored by Terrapin Care Station.
 “The Merry + Bright Market has always been about making the holidays a little easier and more joyful for the families we’ve served,” said Emily Gorski, founder and executive director of DIG Furniture Bank. “This year, we’re excited to be sponsored by Terrapin Care Station, allowing us to purchase brand-new gifts for children of DIG families among other special touches to make the day memorable.”
 DIG recently announced plans to relocate from its Milton facility to a new building, where it will have an opportunity to improve its operations, volunteer experience and services to families across Snyder, Union and Northumberland counties. The market will be the final community event at the current location before DIG’s lease ends in December.
 “Moving is a big undertaking, but we’re excited about what it means for the future of DIG,” Gorski said. “Before we go, we want to make sure as many items as possible find a good home.”
 Founded in 2020, DIG Furniture Bank provides gently used furniture and household essentials at no cost to individuals and families in need. It has furnished the homes of more than 1,000 local families, according to the organization. More information is at DIG Furniture Bank’s website .
